realLife.title: Hotel check-in
realLife.opening: Good evening. Do you have a reservation?

steps.task: Say you booked a room for tonight.
options: Yes, I have a reservation for tonight.
Yes, I am having a reserve tonight.
steps.explanation: The present simple describes an existing booking.

steps.task: Ask when breakfast starts.
steps.explanation: Use does before the subject in a present simple question.

steps.task: Ask politely if you may leave luggage after checkout.
options: Can I leaving my luggage here tomorrow?
Could I leave my luggage here after checking out?
steps.explanation: Could I + base verb is a polite request.

realLife.title: At the café
realLife.opening: Hi! Are you ready to order?

steps.task: Order a latte politely.
options: Could I have a latte, please?
steps.explanation: Could I have ... is a natural polite request.

steps.task: Ask whether oat milk is available.
steps.explanation: Do you have ... asks if the shop offers something.

steps.task: Ask for the check.
options: Could we have the check, please?
steps.explanation: Check is common US English in a restaurant.

realLife.title: At the airport
realLife.opening: May I see your boarding pass?

steps.task: Explain that your pass is on your phone.
options: It is in my telephone inside.
I have it in phone me.
steps.explanation: On my phone is an idiomatic location phrase.

steps.task: Ask where your gate is.
options: Could you tell me where my gate is?
Could you tell me where is my gate?
steps.explanation: Indirect questions keep normal subject–verb order.

steps.task: Ask whether the flight is delayed.
steps.explanation: Be + subject + adjective/past participle.

realLife.title: Finding your way
realLife.opening: Excuse me, are you looking for something?

steps.task: Ask how to get to the subway.
options: How I can get to subway?
How can I get to the subway station?
steps.explanation: Use can before the subject.

steps.task: Ask how long the walk takes.
options: How much time it taking for walk?
How long does it take to walk there?
How long it take to walk?
steps.explanation: How long does it take ... is common for duration.

steps.task: Check that you understood the directions.
options: So I turn left at the next street, right?
So I will left from next street?
steps.explanation: A confirmation question can check understanding.

realLife.title: Meeting a neighbor
realLife.opening: Hi, I just moved into this building.

steps.task: Welcome your neighbor.
steps.explanation: Welcome to + place.

steps.task: Ask how they like the neighborhood.
options: Are you liking the area until now?
How do you like the neighborhood so far?
steps.explanation: How do you like ... so far? is a natural question.

steps.task: Offer to help if they need anything.
options: Let me know if you need anything.
Tell to me if you need something.
steps.explanation: Let me know if ... is a natural offer.

realLife.title: Rescheduling an appointment
realLife.opening: Hello, how can I help you today?

steps.task: Say you need to change your appointment.
options: I am need to switch an appoint.
I need to reschedule my appointment.
steps.explanation: Reschedule is natural for changing a booked time.

steps.task: Ask about available times on Friday.
options: Do you have any openings on Friday?
steps.explanation: Any openings asks about appointment availability.

steps.task: Thank the person for accommodating you.
steps.explanation: Thanks for + noun or -ing form.

realLife.title: Returning an item
realLife.opening: Hello, what can I do for you?

steps.task: Explain that the item does not work.
options: I bought this yesterday, but it does not work.
I buy this yesterday and not working.
steps.explanation: Use bought for a past purchase and does not work for current status.

steps.task: Ask about the return policy.
steps.explanation: Return policy is the store rule about returns.

steps.task: Ask whether you can exchange it.
options: Can I changing it for other?
Could I exchange it for another one?
steps.explanation: Could I + base verb; exchange for another item.

realLife.title: Making weekend plans
realLife.opening: Do you have plans this weekend?

steps.task: Say you are free on Saturday.
options: I am free on Saturday afternoon.
I am free in Saturday afternoon.
steps.explanation: On + day; in + part of day without a named day.

steps.task: Suggest trying a new place.
options: Why we don’t try new restaurant?
Why don’t we try that new restaurant?
steps.explanation: Why don’t we + base verb suggests a plan.

steps.task: Ask what time works best.
options: What time works best for you?
What time to you is best working?
steps.explanation: What time works best for you? is natural.

realLife.title: Starting a conversation
realLife.opening: That is a nice book. What are you reading?

steps.task: Say what kind of book it is.
steps.explanation: It is + a + singular countable noun.

steps.task: Ask what books the other person likes.
options: What kind of books do you enjoy?
steps.explanation: What kind of + plural noun; do you + base verb.

steps.task: Ask for a recommendation.
steps.explanation: Recommend + object is natural here.

realLife.title: Calling customer support
realLife.opening: Thanks for calling. What seems to be the problem?

steps.task: Explain the package has not arrived.
options: My package has not arrived yet.
My package did not arrived yet.
steps.explanation: Present perfect is natural when it has not arrived up to now.

steps.task: Ask when it will arrive.
options: Do you know when it will arrive?
Do you know when will it arrive?
When it will arrive you know?
steps.explanation: Use statement word order inside indirect questions.

steps.task: Ask for a tracking number.
options: Could you give me the tracking number?
steps.explanation: Could you + base verb.

realLife.title: At the pharmacy
realLife.opening: Hello. What are you looking for?

steps.task: Ask where the sunscreen is.
options: Where I can find the sunscreen?
steps.explanation: Where can I + base verb.

steps.task: Ask about the price.
steps.explanation: How much + does + singular subject + base verb.

steps.task: Ask if there is a smaller size.
options: Do you have a smaller size?
steps.explanation: Do you have ... is a common shopping question.

realLife.title: Asking a classmate
realLife.opening: Hi! Did you understand today’s lesson?

steps.task: Admit that you missed one part.
options: I understood most of it, but I missed the last part.
I understanded all but missed last.
I am missing the last part yesterday.
steps.explanation: Past tense: understood, missed.

steps.task: Ask for an explanation.
options: Could you explain that part again?
steps.explanation: Explain is a verb: could you explain ...

steps.task: Ask to study together.
options: Would you like to study together tomorrow?
steps.explanation: Would you like to + base verb.

thinking.task: Politely decline a dinner invitation and give one reason.
thinking.modelAnswer: Thanks for inviting me, but I already have plans that evening.

thinking.task: You did not understand a direction. Ask for clarification.
thinking.modelAnswer: Could you explain which street I should turn onto?

thinking.task: A friend is starting a new course. Ask a thoughtful follow-up question.
thinking.modelAnswer: What made you choose that course?

thinking.task: Give your opinion about working from home, with one reason.
thinking.modelAnswer: I think working from home can be helpful because it saves commuting time.

thinking.task: Compare taking the train with driving for a weekend trip.
thinking.modelAnswer: The train is often more relaxing, whereas driving gives you more flexibility.

thinking.task: Apologize for being late and explain briefly.
thinking.modelAnswer: I am sorry I am late. The bus was delayed.

thinking.task: Ask to move a meeting to next Monday.
thinking.modelAnswer: Would it be possible to move our meeting to next Monday?

thinking.task: Ask what someone would do if they had a free month.
thinking.modelAnswer: What would you do if you had a whole month off?

thinking.task: Say that something was expensive but worth buying.
thinking.modelAnswer: Although it was expensive, I think it was worth buying.

thinking.task: Explain why you decided to learn a new skill.
thinking.modelAnswer: I decided to learn a new skill because I want to challenge myself.

thinking.task: Ask someone for details about their weekend plans.
thinking.modelAnswer: What are you planning to do on Saturday afternoon?

thinking.task: Say you are not certain, then suggest how to check.
thinking.modelAnswer: I am not sure, but we could check the official website.

thinking.task: Recommend a quiet place to read.
thinking.modelAnswer: I would recommend the library because it is usually peaceful.

thinking.task: Agree with a proposal and add a benefit.
thinking.modelAnswer: That sounds reasonable, and it could also save us time.

thinking.task: Disagree politely with an idea and explain why.
thinking.modelAnswer: I see your point, but I think we need more information.

thinking.task: Say that you will join a trip if the weather is good.
thinking.modelAnswer: I will join you as long as the weather is good.

thinking.task: Ask a classmate to send you the notes.
thinking.modelAnswer: Could you send me your notes when you have a moment?

thinking.task: Check whether you understood someone correctly.
thinking.modelAnswer: Do you mean that we should arrive before nine?

thinking.task: Explain why you prefer studying in the morning.
thinking.modelAnswer: I prefer studying in the morning because I can concentrate better.

thinking.task: Tell someone about a small unexpected event yesterday.
thinking.modelAnswer: Yesterday I missed my bus, so I walked to the station.

thinking.task: Describe a plan for learning English next month.
thinking.modelAnswer: Next month I am going to practice listening every morning.

thinking.task: Use a question tag to check a plan.
thinking.modelAnswer: We are meeting at seven, aren’t we?

thinking.task: Ask politely where the nearest pharmacy is.
thinking.modelAnswer: Could you tell me where the nearest pharmacy is?

thinking.task: Suggest an alternative when a restaurant is full.
thinking.modelAnswer: We could try the café across the street instead.

writing.title: Write a polite email to reschedule a meeting.
writing.instructions: Explain the conflict, suggest two possible times, and end politely.

writing.title: Write to customer service about a delayed order.
writing.instructions: Give the order context, explain the issue, and request a specific solution.

writing.title: Should students have homework every day?
writing.instructions: Give an opinion, two reasons, one example, and a conclusion.

writing.title: Describe something you learned from a mistake.
writing.instructions: Describe what happened, the result, and what you would do differently.

writing.title: Compare online and face-to-face courses.
writing.instructions: Compare their advantages and disadvantages and explain your preference.

writing.title: Invite a friend to an event.
writing.instructions: Include when, where, why it could be fun, and how to respond.

writing.title: Does technology always save time?
writing.instructions: Consider at least one counterargument before your conclusion.

writing.title: Write a short review of a café you visited.
writing.instructions: Describe atmosphere, service, value, and whether you recommend it.

writing.title: Suggest an improvement to a local park.
writing.instructions: Describe a problem, propose a solution, and explain a benefit.

writing.title: Explain how you would plan a three-day city trip.
writing.instructions: Include priorities, transport options, and a backup plan.

writing.title: Write an email apologizing for missing a deadline.
writing.instructions: Take responsibility, explain briefly, and suggest a concrete next step.

writing.title: Tell a story about meeting someone unexpectedly.
writing.instructions: Include background, a turning point, and an ending.
